N. |date=2001-04-16 |title=Tose Undertakes Multiple GameCube Projects |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2001/04/16/tose-undertakes-multiple-gamecube-projects |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=IGN |language=en}} It also does non-games work, developing software for the web, mobile apps, [[pachinko]] machines, and even appliances, like refrigerators.{{Cite web |last=Leone |first=Matt |date=2015-09-30 |title=The secret developers of the video game industry |url=https://www.polygon.com/2015/9/30/9394355/the-secret-developers-of-the-video-game-industry/ |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Polygon |language=en}} ==History== Tose was established by Shigeru Saito in November 1979 in [[Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto|Higashiyama-ku]], [[Kyoto]], as an independent entity of his father's company Toa Seiko Co., Ltd.{{Cite web |title=会社沿革｜東亜セイコー｜Toa Seiko Ltd. |url=https://www.toaseiko.com/company/history/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=www.toaseiko.com |language=ja}} At the time, Toa Seiko had a contract to produce arcade cabinets for ''[[Space Invaders]]'', but its other clients complained about being associated with the gaming industry. It began as an arcade cabinet manufacturer with only five employees. Its first game was the arcade game [[Sasuke vs. Commander|''Sasuke vs. Commande''r]] for [[SNK]] in September 1980.{{Cite news |last=Sheffield |first=Brandon |date=April 20, 2007 |title=Tose: Game Development Ninjas II - Battle for the West |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/tose-game-development-ninjas-ii---battle-for-the-west |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207085512/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/tose-game-development-ninjas-ii---battle-for-the-west |archive-date=2025-02-07 |access-date=2025-12-14 |work=Game Developer |language=en}} It released [[Vanguard (video game)|''Vanguard'']], a side-scrolling shooter, in March 1981.{{Cite web |title=History {{!}} About Us {{!}} TOSE CO., LTD. |url=https://www.tose.co.jp/en/company/history.html |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=www.tose.co.jp}} ''[[Vanguard II (video game)|Vanguard II]]'', a top-down sequel was made in three years later. By 1982, the company transitioned to software development. When the [[Nintendo Entertainment System|Famicom]] released in 1983, Tose was able to partner with Nintendo because it already had experience developing for the console's CPU. It worked with [[Taito]] to port ''[[Space Invaders]]'' to the console, and also worked on ''[[Kid Icarus]],'' as well as the ''[[Dragon Ball]]'' video game series.{{Cite web |date=June 2008 |title=Interview: Daniel Auld |url=https://gdri.smspower.org/wiki/index.php/Interview:Daniel_Auld |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=Game Developer Research Institute |language=en}} By this point, Tose had built a reputation as a reliable development partner for third-party titles.{{Cite web |last=Cassidy |date=2020-05-29 |title=Spelunker (NES) |url=https://www.badgamehalloffame.com/spelunker-nes/ |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=Bad Game Hall of Fame |language=en-US}} The company moved its head office to Otokuni-gun, Kyoto Prefecture in May 1986 and Saito was named president. Saito was named president of the company in February 1987. In July 1988, a new head office was completed in[[Yamazaki]], Kyoto. In May 1990, Tose began developing software for the [[Game Boy]] and the [[Super Famicom]]. In 1993, Tose opened offices in [[Shanghai|Shanghai, China]]{{Cite web |author=noguchi |date=July 15, 2007 |script-title=ja:［CJ 2007＃43］臭い息？ お母さん召喚？ ある意味派手なアイテムが満載のオンラインサッカーゲーム「蹴蹴球」 |url=https://www.4gamer.net/games/041/G004155/20070715234803/ |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=4Gamer.net |language=ja }} and [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]]. The US subsidiary dissolved soon after. During this time, the company began developing mobile games from [[NTT Docomo]]'s [[i-mode]]. In August 1999, Tose was listed on the [[Osaka Exchange|Osaka Securities Exchange]] 2nd Section and the Kyoto Stock Exchange. In October of that year, Tose's Kyoto head office was opened at Shijo-Karasuma. In September 2000, Tose was listed on the [[Tokyo Stock Exchange]] 2nd Section.{{Cite web |date=2007-10-27 |title=TOSE Software-Japan- |url=http://www.tose.co.jp/jp/ir/2000/000927.html |access-date=2023-04-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027055016/http://www.tose.co.jp/jp/ir/2000/000927.html |archive-date=2007-10-27 |language=ja}} A second subsidiary based in China was established in [[Hangzhou]] in March 2001. In August, Tose was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange 1st Section and Osaka Securities Exchange 1st Section. A new office was opened in [[Shibuya|Shibuya-ku, Tokyo]] in September 2002. Following six years of development, Tose partnered with Nintendo in 2002 to release [[Densetsu no Starfy (video game)|''Densetsu no Starfy'']] for the Game Boy Advance. This was the company's first original IP.{{Cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Chris |last2=Slate |first2=Chris |date=August 2009 |title=A Star is (Re)Born |url=http://www.nintendopower.com/images/NP244_Starfy.jpg |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714184528/http://www.nintendopower.com/images/NP244_Starfy.jpg |archive-date=2011-07-14 |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Nintendo Power |page=73 |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Dillard |first=Corbie |date=2009-05-22 |title=Interviews: Nintendo/TOSE - The Legendary Starfy |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2009/05/interviews_nintendotose_the_legendary_starfy |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB}} Tose re-entered the US market in March 2003 and was able to establish an office [[Westlake Village, California]]{{Cite web |title=Tose Software USA Inc. |url=http://www.tose-us.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050112021714/http://www.tose-us.com/ |archive-date=January 12, 2005}} with just two employees.{{Cite news |last=Sheffield |first=Brandon |date=August 24, 2008 |title=Return Of The Ninja: Tose's Stealthy Outsourcing Progress |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/game-platforms/return-of-the-ninja-tose-s-stealthy-outsourcing-progress |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250212210220/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/game-platforms/return-of-the-ninja-tose-s-stealthy-outsourcing-progress |archive-date=2025-02-12 |access-date=2025-12-14 |work=Game Developer |language=en}} Saito was named CEO in September 2004. In October, the company established Phoenix Communications as a subsidiary in Tokyo to plan, develop, sell, and manage digital content for the web. By 2006, 70% of Tose's clients were located in Japan, 15% in China, 10% in the U.S., and 5% Korea, Canada, and other regions. It had six studios across Japan, China, and the United States with 800 employees in Japan and 200 in China. On December 18, 2007, Tose announced the leakage of its business information onto the Internet, which was discovered the day before. The leak included 10 pieces of information relating to customer names, development cases, development contents, development fees, and reception time.[http://www.tose.co.jp/jp/ir/pdf/20071218.pdf 業務情報の漏洩に関するお知らせ]{{Dead link|date=July 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }} By 2008, Tose had opened additional studios in Okinawa, Nagoya, and Sapporo, and expanded to 1,000 employees in Japan alone. After four installments of the Starfy series in Japan, 2009's ''[[The Legendary Starfy (video game)|The Legendary Starfy]]'' on the Nintendo DS was the first game to release in North America.{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Peer |date=2024-07-12 |title=Starfy: Kirby's Brother From Another Mother |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/starfy-kirbys-brother-from-another-mother |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=IGN |language=en}} Tose designed the game to be accessible for Western audiences.{{Cite web |last=DeVries |first=Jack |date=2009-05-22 |title=Developers Talk Legendary Starfy Details |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2009/05/22/developers-talk-legendary-starfy-details |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=IGN |language=en}} By 2011, the company was producing 110-120 titles each year. On September 1, 2011, Tose announced the separation of its amusement machine development business from its second game development department (ゲーム事業部開発2部) into a separate amusement machine developer (AM開発部).{{Cite web| date=2011-10-30 | title=機構改革および人事異動についてのお知らせ | language=ja | trans-title=Notice regarding organizational reform and personnel changes | url=http://www.tose.co.jp/jp/ir/pdf/20110901.pdf | access-date=2023-04-19 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111030210427/http://www.tose.co.jp/jp/ir/pdf/20110901.pdf | archive-date=2011-10-30 }} By 2012, Tose had 12 offices across three countries. Business in the US market had been declining following the end of development for Wii and DS games. In order to diversify its efforts, Tose chose to publish its first game, ''Susume Tactics!'' for Sony's [[PlayStation Portable|PSP]]. In June 2013, Tose dissolved its US subsidiary and opened an office in [[Manila|Manila, Philippines]].{{Cite web |date=2015-11-17 |title=Dossier - A Kyoto, Nintendo est aussi indispensable que discret |url=https://www.gamekult.com/actualite/kyoto-stories-nintendo-et-apres-155845.html |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=www.gamekult.com |language=fr}} In 2014, the company restructured its development teams.{{Cite web |author=津久井箇人 |date=2014-08-25 |script-title=ja:ゲーム業界の「縁の下の力持ち」トーセが開発体制を改革 ― 時代に適応した事業体制の見直しと新事業部創設 |url=https://www.inside-games.jp/article/2014/08/25/79812.html |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=インサイド |language=ja}} By 2015, the company had 400 employees in China and Philippines. Saito became chairman in 2015, while Yasuhito Watanabe was appointed as president and COO.{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2015 |title=トーセ、12月1日付で取締役兼COOの渡辺康人氏が代表取締役社長に就任へ 現・代表取締役社長の齋藤茂氏は代表取締役会長に {{!}} gamebiz |url=https://gamebiz.jp/news/150769 |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=gamebiz【ゲームビズ】 |language=ja}} By 2023, video games accounted for 70% of the company's business, while the remaining 30% came from mobile content.{{Cite web |date=2023-01-30 |author=不破聡 |title=受託開発専門企業トーセは平均より低い給与水準が経営リスクにならないか？【ゲーム企業の決算を読む】 |url=https://www.gamebusiness.jp/article/2023/01/30/21289.html |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=GameBusiness.jp |language=ja }} In July 2024, the first three Starfy games were added to the [[Nintendo Classics]] collection as part of the [[Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack]] subscription.{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2024 |title=More games added to the NES and Game Boy Advance collections |url=https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/new-update-see-what-games-were-added-to-the-nes-and-game-boy-advance-collections/ |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=www.nintendo.com |language=en-US}} It was reported that Tose was experiencing financial hardship due to a number of cancelled games from partners including [[Square Enix]] and [[Bandai Namco Holdings|Bandai Namco]]. Tose Co., Ltd. (also called Tose Software) is a Japanese video game developer based in Kyoto. It is mostly known for developing Nintendo's Game & Watch Gallery series, various Dragon Ball games, as well as contract work or assistance to other developers. Tose has developed or co-developed thousands of games since the company's inception in 1979, but is virtually never credited in the games themselves. It is considered the largest non-publishing game developer in the world.
Tose maintains a policy of having no creative input in the games it works on, going so far as to refuse to put the studio's name in the credits and employees using pseudonyms in its early days. As such, Tose has gained a reputation for being a "ghost developer." Representatives of the company have described it as a "ninja developer," because it works in the shadows, as well as the "unsung hero" of the video game industry. When talking to the press, representatives of the company ask not to be identified by name. Exceptions to this include Game & Watch Gallery 4 and The Legendary Starfy series, as Tose shares the copyright with Nintendo.
The company provides services for game design, plot design, sound composition, programming, and more. It also does non-games work, developing software for the web, mobile apps, pachinko machines, and even appliances, like refrigerators.
